title: Origin story: Hermes
description: Hermes was the son of Zeus and the nymph Maia, born in a cave on Mount Cyllene. On his first day of life he invented the lyre from a tortoise shell and stole Apollo's cattle, walking them backward to confuse trackers. Amused rather than angry, Apollo made him the gods' herald, and Zeus gave him the caduceus.

description: Powers: Winged sandals and cap for flight beyond wind; The caduceus, which puts mortals to sleep or wakes them; Free passage across every boundary — even death's.

title: Stamina feats: Hermes
description: Recorded feats of endurance: Runs the gods' messages across the world without pause; Sleeps less than any god, always in motion.

title: Cultural impact: Hermes
description: Patron of merchants, travelers, and tricksters; his caduceus is the emblem of commerce.
